SINAMICS Startdrive G110M, G120, G120C, G120D, G120P, G115D

Comment.MultiLanguageText: Caller-visible interface (C-115) - FC_ControlMain writes Mode/HopperHighLevel/limits/tunables in, reads Extend/Retract/RunPowerPack/fault bits out. See the block header for the Step/Mode value legend.

Named once, read everywhere (C-601): the live cycle trigger - Auto on hopper high or Manual on the HMI button - gated by Enable (Fitted AND not Off) and NOT Blocked. Read by the warning armer, the launch and repark transitions, and the trip-count reset. Blocked is written later in the scan, so this reads it one scan behind - immaterial: Blocked can only latch mid-stroke (Step 10) where no Step 0 request can act, and a reset-clear merely delays a relaunch by one scan.

A live jog request: either jog button held, idle, Manual mode, pusher fitted. Arms the pre-motion warning, suppresses the repark (jogging is never fought by an auto-retract), and - per direction, warning done - drives the demands. Reads Step from before this scan's transitions; the demand rungs re-check Step fresh.

A repark to home is wanted: the sequencer's pre-start ParkCmd (REQ-045) or a live CycleRequest, while idle off home and not jogging. One of the only two motion sources out of Step 0 (owner ruling 2026-07-16); fires the 0-to-30 transition once the pre-motion warning has sounded.

A cycle launch is possible: live CycleRequest, idle, ram at home. Fires the 0-to-10 transition once the pre-motion warning has sounded; the same fired condition resets PressureTripCount (per-cycle jam counting, REQ-048).

Named once (C-601): abort an in-flight cycle to Retract - Off commanded mid-cycle, or the plant acquired a stop reason (CycleInhibit). Read by the Step 10 and Step 20 exits; the Step 30 retract completes regardless, so an aborted cycle always ends parked. Jog is untouched by this bit (owner amendment 2026-07-16).
Latched jam hold, not a fault (C-123) - see the Pressure Detection network. Freezes ExtendDemand while set; clears itself once pressure has genuinely stayed clear for PressureClearResumeDelay.
Confirmed jams this cycle - reset each cycle start, not time-windowed. Compared against IO.PressureTripCountThreshold to raise Blocked.
ExtendDemand OR RetractDemand - the pump's own immediate (non-run-on) demand signal.
Cold-start guard for the pump run-on off-delay below - see that network's own comment.

AttributeList.Text: Pusher ram sequencing (C-118-C-125). Step legend (C-120): 0=Idle (no motion; home is the HomeLimit switch, not implied by the step - after a jog release the ram may legitimately rest off home, REQ-039) - 10=DriveToEndTravel (forward stroke in progress) - 20=Hold (paused at full travel, brief settle before retracting) - 30=Retract (returning to home; also the recovery/abort target from any bad state). Mode legend: 0=Off (finish a retract already in progress, then park; no new cycle starts) - 1=Auto (hopper-high-level starts a cycle) - 2=Manual (operator button/jog starts a cycle). Motion policy (owner rulings 2026-07-16): an idle off-home ram reparks ONLY on the plant pre-start ParkCmd or on a live cycle request - never on jog release or bare mode changes - and every motion start from rest (repark, cycle launch, jog) is preceded by the JogWarningTime sounder warning (NEW-4: no unwarned pusher motion). CycleInhibit (any live plant stop reason) blocks cycle launches and aborts an in-flight cycle to park, but deliberately leaves hand-jog available - only the mode-0 force (stop button/unhealthy) blocks jogging (owner amendment 2026-07-16, REQ-040). Fitted=FALSE (REQ-042/043/044) kills every demand, the pack output, both supervision timers, and every fault latch at the source, so a disabled pusher does nothing and raises nothing.

The compound conditions every later network shares, each written once (C-601). Requests read Step as it settled last scan (the transitions run later) - safe, because Step only ever leaves 0 through this scan's own request-gated transitions; steps returning to 0 just re-arm the requests one scan late. CycleInhibit kills cycle requests (no launch into a stopped plant) and, via CycleAbort, retracts an in-flight cycle - while JogDemand deliberately ignores it: hand-jog stays available with the plant stopped by downstream absence (owner amendment 2026-07-16, REQ-040).
Enable And Motion Requests

Fitted gates both the set and the hold of the latch (REQ-043/044, gate at the source): a disabled pusher raises no fault, and a fault latched while fitted clears the moment the pusher is disabled. FC_AlarmsMain reads only these already-gated bits.
Both Limit Switches Active Simultaneously

HMI/DB_Settings times are Real seconds for operator legibility; every TON below needs its PT in DInt ms - one MUL+CONVERT pair per timer, matching the MotorDOL FTTime/EnableUPSTime idiom. Kept as one block up front rather than repeated at each timer, so the x1000 idiom is visibly consistent and only ever done once.
HMI Time Conversions

NEW-4 owner ruling (2026-07-16): no unwarned pusher motion. Every motion start from rest - repark, auto/manual cycle launch, jog - arms this timer and the sounder; the Step 0 transitions and the jog demands only act on its Q, so the sounder always leads motion by JogWarningTime. Jog keeps sounding while moving (REQ-041) because JogDemand stays true through the jog; in-cycle strokes (10/20/30, including a stop-forced retract) are continuations of an already-warned launch, so the warning boundary is Step 0. A request released mid-warning (short manual tap, hopper clearing) simply never moves. Timer and sounder keep their original jog-era names to avoid interface churn - rename queued with the cosmetic pass.
Pre-Motion Warning

One function, one network: a trip must be debounced (PressureConfirmTimer) before it counts - momentary pressure spikes aren't a real jam. Hold latches through a confirmed trip and only releases once pressure has genuinely cleared for PressureClearResumeDelay, so a bouncing switch can't re-trigger the count on every scan. Count resets each cycle start (the same LaunchRequest-and-warning-done condition that fires the 0-to-10 launch), not on a rolling time window.
Pressure Trip Detection, Hold, And Counting
Fitted gates set and hold (REQ-043/044, gate at the source) - a disabled pusher raises nothing, and disabling clears a standing latch.
Blocked Fault (Too Many Jams)

Repark (0 to 30) fires only on a live occasion - the plant pre-start ParkCmd (REQ-045) or a cycle request arriving with the ram off home - and only after the pre-motion warning has sounded. Jog release deliberately triggers nothing: the ram stops and stays where it is (REQ-039, owner ruling 2026-07-16), and Off mode alone no longer self-parks an idle ram either - it parks at the next pre-start or cycle request. Launch (0 to 10) still requires the ram at home; a request with the ram off home reparks first, then launches if the request is still live at home. The two exits are mutually exclusive by construction (NOT HomeLimit vs HomeLimit, C-121).
Step 0 (Idle) - Warned Repark And Launch

Every abnormal exit - CycleAbort (Off commanded mid-stroke, or the plant acquired a stop reason), or a timeout, whether or not it also trips Blocked - goes straight to Retract (30), never a bare stop; the ram is never left sitting mid-travel. Only reaching FullTravelLimit cleanly goes to Hold (20) first, per the normal cycle. Fitted gates the supervision timer (a disabled pusher looks for no switch feedback, REQ-043) and the fault latch (raises nothing, REQ-044).
Step 10 (Drive To End Travel) - Timer, Timeout Fault, And Transitions
Step 20 (Hold) - Timer And Transition

ParkedTimer's own Q only feeds the timeout fault, not a transition - if genuinely stuck retracting there's no safer step to force (unlike Step 10, nothing here can be aborted into); alarm-only by design, awaiting a human. Fitted gates the supervision timer and the fault latch (REQ-043/044) - a disabled pusher neither watches for the home switch nor raises the fault.
Step 30 (Retract) - Timer, Timeout Fault, And Transition

PressureHold gates ExtendDemand so a confirmed jam holds the ram in place rather than continuing to push (a hold per C-123, not a fault - it clears and driving resumes the instant pressure has cleared). Jog demand arms only after the pre-motion warning (JogPreStartTimer.Q via NETWORK 4) and re-checks Step = 0 fresh: JogDemand was computed before this scan's transitions, so a same-scan launch or repark must still kill the jog demand rather than drive both solenoids for a scan. Every term is Fitted-gated (REQ-043: a disabled pusher never demands motion) - the cycle terms explicitly, the jog terms through JogDemand's own gate.
Extend And Retract Demand
Pump Demand

Off-delay built from TON+inversion, not TOF/TONR (C-406). PumpEverDemanded guards a cold-start gap: on power-up PumpDemand and the timer's Q are both initially false, which would read as 'run-on already elapsed' and skip straight to no-run. RunPowerPack stays on through the run-on tail even after demand drops, but the Extend/Retract solenoids are not - they only ever follow live demand, gated by PowerPackRunningFB so the ram can't be commanded before the pump has confirmed running. Fitted gates RunPowerPack directly too: disabling the pusher must kill the pack immediately, run-on tail included (REQ-043).
